note: Order every 2 days at about 1.08 × forecast for item 0 and 1.05 × forecast for item 1, which halves the order fees; risk: a random demand spike between orders leaves no stock.
Order every day at 1.1 × / 1.05 × the forecast for the arrival day; risk: the order fees (about 1,560 total) eat into profit.
Lean version of ordering every 2 days (1.0 × / 0.95 × forecast); risk: more shortage penalties, because average demand runs about 4.6% above the forecast.
Generous version of ordering every 2 days (1.18 × / 1.12 × forecast); risk: item 1 expires after 5 days, plus storage costs and leftovers at the end.
Order every 3 days at about 1.06 × / 1.03 × forecast, the lowest order fees; risk: high storage cost for item 1, the 316-unit capacity limit, and longer gaps for demand swings.
Lean daily orders (1.0 × / 0.95 × forecast); risk: shortages plus the full order fees.
Every 2 days with uneven safety stock: 1.12 × forecast for item 0 (shortages are costly) and 1.0 × for item 1 (perishable, waste is costly); risk: shortages of item 1 on high-demand days.
Generous daily orders (1.2 × / 1.15 × forecast); risk: order fees plus write-offs and storage costs, especially for item 1.
